newsitem.title: UK: Britain may outlaw chequebook journalism in trials.
newsitem.headline: Britain may outlaw chequebook journalism in trials.

text.p: Britain took the first step on Tuesday toward outlawing "chequebook journalism" payments to trial witnesses.
Newspapers and television stations set alarm bells ringing by paying 19 witnesses sums of up to 20,000 pounds ($30,000) before last year's "House of Horrors" trial of serial killer Rosemary West.

Lord Mackay of Clashfern, the lord chancellor, said the government feared that witnesses might omit something from their evidence to make a media exclusive or exaggerate evidence to make their stories more newsworthy.

"The government considers that such payments can constitute a real risk to the administration of justice," Mackay said in a statement inviting views by the end of the year on a proposal to ban payments.
